tools.name: create_experiment

Give `instructions` with goal, variables, language, brand, audience, lockedConstraints and a `direction` that is the whole spec (per-slide scene and exact overlay copy, up to {DIRECTION_MAX} characters; required), plus slideCount (3–8, the real output length, not clamped to any source), variantCount and maxCredits. It still creates a free draft with a planEstimate and follows plan_experiment â review â generate_experiment with the same approval gates; planning skips source analysis.
• mode "create" (default) — one experiment PER source video, because briefs never mix sources, so N videoIds create N drafts. Give `instructions`: what to vary, the goal, optional creative direction. Pass `instructions.preserveSourceCtaSlide: true` to keep a source deck's own closing call-to-action slide in the deck.
• mode "edit" — exactly ONE deck. For a character-only edit pass variables:["character"] and `character` (visible casting direction); omit hook/overlayTexts to keep all source copy, style, setting and story locked. For a scene edit pass variables:["scene"] and `scene` (one description for every slide, or one per slide): each slide is an edit of the baseline slide that keeps the same person, outfit, pose, medium, lighting, camera and overlay text and changes only the setting and props (the baseline stays the source deck); omit hook/overlayTexts. For a copy edit (variables:["hook"], default), keep the same images and pass `hook` (slide 1) and `overlayTexts` (slides 2, 3, â¦ in order; an empty string strips that slide's text, null leaves it unchanged) instead of `instructions`; the tool assembles the same brief the site sends — fixed goal, one selected variable, controlled mode, 2 variants, a 200-credit cap â with the copy quoted per slide in the site's wording. The source deck's own slide count wins when it is known; pass slideCount only if you do not have it.
Sources must be slideshows or videos with a finished Recreate deck (show_gallery marks them). Photo-annotation videos (face photo + drawn line + ✅/❌ badge + score card) are also accepted: their deck is drawn in code from the tagged face library at 0 image credits. The first call queues that render and returns composite_deck_pending with a job id; await the job and repeat the same call. Shape the deck with `composite`. Credits: analysis {CREDIT_COSTS.analyzeVideo}/source + {CREDIT_COSTS.experimentPlanningCall} per planning call at plan time; Multiplying one deck: in create mode, instructions.mode "exploration" with several variables (hook, character, concept, scene) and variantCount 6-12 returns the baseline plus variantCount-1 alternates, each one a different combination of those variables (single-variable controls first, then mixes); "controlled" keeps each alternate to one variable. plan-stage estimates carry projectedGenerationCredits (upperBound: true), the ceiling if every alternate re-rendered every slide. {CREDIT_COSTS.experimentSlide} per slide render at generation: one render per slide, and slides an alternate shares with the baseline are free. A QA check of each deck ({CREDIT_COSTS.experimentPlanningCall}) is added, and estimate_experiment(stage="generate") gives the exact total. Experiment lifecycle: create_experiment (draft, free) → estimate_experiment stage=plan → user approves → plan_experiment (background: source analysis, pattern report, variant briefs) → status "review" → optionally update_experiment_variant → estimate_experiment stage=generate → user approves → generate_experiment (background slide rendering) → "completed". Approval: a spending step needs the user's OK, and a standing budget IS that OK. If the task or user granted a credit cap (per experiment or per batch), any estimate within the remaining cap is already approved: pass the remaining cap (or the estimate) as approvedCredits and run plan → generate without asking again. Without a cap, ask ONCE for all experiments and both stages together, not per experiment or per stage. Ask again only when an estimate exceeds what was approved. To change a brief, use update_experiment_variant (free) rather than cancel_experiment.

mode.description: "create" (default) = new variations from source videos plus instructions. "edit" = change overlay copy or character on one deck. "brief" = no source video: generate from instructions alone.

videoIds.description: Required in create and edit modes: 1–20 distinct Gallery video ids; one experiment per video. Edit mode takes exactly one. Must be omitted in brief mode.

instructions.description: CREATE and BRIEF modes. Required in both; rejected in edit mode (use top-level variables and character or hook/overlayTexts). Brief mode also requires instructions.direction.

variables.description: EDIT mode: ["hook"] for copy, ["character"] for casting only, ["scene"] for the setting, or ["morph"] (alias "ladder") to re-create a tier-ladder deck with one invented subject graded slide by slide, labels drawn in code. Defaults to scene when scene is supplied, then character when character is supplied, then morph when morph is supplied, otherwise hook.

scene.description: EDIT mode, scene variable: where the deck takes place instead (setting and props). One description for every slide, or an array with one per slide. Keeps the same person, outfit, pose, medium, lighting, camera and overlay text. Omit hook/overlayTexts/character.

morph.description: EDIT mode, morph variable: the progression to test in neutral visible words, optionally with per-slide grades 0-4 (e.g. "jaw definition 4,4,3,3,2,1,0; cheek fullness 0,0,1,2,3,3,4"). Omit to follow the source frames.

character.description: EDIT mode, character variable: visible casting changes (e.g. short blond hair). Keeps source copy, style, setting and story. Omit hook/overlayTexts.

hook.description: EDIT mode: the exact words for slide 1. OMIT this field to leave slide 1 unchanged; send an empty string only to strip slide 1's text.

overlayTexts.description: EDIT mode: overlay text for slides 2, 3, â¦ in order. Empty string = render no text on that slide. null = leave that slide's original text unchanged (use it to skip a slide between two you are editing).

tools.name: create_experiment
tools.description:
Create draft experiment(s). Free â a draft spends nothing. Three modes, matching the site's experiment wizard (source choices: Gallery slideshows, one slideshow to edit, or no source at all):
• mode "brief" — NO source video. One experiment generated from a written brief. Do not pass videoIds. Give `instructions` with goal, variables, language, brand, audience, lockedConstraints and a `direction` that is the whole spec (per-slide scene and exact overlay copy, up to {DIRECTION_MAX} characters; required), plus slideCount (3–8, the real output length, not clamped to any source), variantCount and maxCredits. It still creates a free draft with a planEstimate and follows plan_experiment â review â generate_experiment with the same approval gates; planning skips source analysis.
• mode "create" (default) — one experiment PER source video, because briefs never mix sources, so N videoIds create N drafts. Give `instructions`: what to vary, the goal, optional creative direction. Pass `instructions.preserveSourceCtaSlide: true` to keep a source deck's own closing call-to-action slide in the deck.
• mode "edit" — exactly ONE deck. For a character-only edit pass variables:["character"] and `character` (visible casting direction); omit hook/overlayTexts to keep all source copy, style, setting and story locked. For a scene edit pass variables:["scene"] and `scene` (one description for every slide, or one per slide): each slide is an edit of the baseline slide that keeps the same person, outfit, pose, medium, lighting, camera and overlay text and changes only the setting and props (the baseline stays the source deck); omit hook/overlayTexts. For a copy edit (variables:["hook"], default), keep the same images and pass `hook` (slide 1) and `overlayTexts` (slides 2, 3, â¦ in order; an empty string strips that slide's text, null leaves it unchanged) instead of `instructions`; the tool assembles the same brief the site sends — fixed goal, one selected variable, controlled mode, 2 variants, a 200-credit cap â with the copy quoted per slide in the site's wording. The source deck's own slide count wins when it is known; pass slideCount only if you do not have it.
Sources must be slideshows or videos with a finished Recreate deck (show_gallery marks them). Photo-annotation videos (face photo + drawn line + ✅/❌ badge + score card) are also accepted: their deck is drawn in code from the tagged face library at 0 image credits. The first call queues that render and returns composite_deck_pending with a job id; await the job and repeat the same call. Shape the deck with `composite`. Credits: analysis {CREDIT_COSTS.analyzeVideo}/source + {CREDIT_COSTS.experimentPlanningCall} per planning call at plan time; Multiplying one deck: in create mode, instructions.mode "exploration" with several variables (hook, character, concept, scene) and variantCount 6-12 returns the baseline plus variantCount-1 alternates, each one a different combination of those variables (single-variable controls first, then mixes); "controlled" keeps each alternate to one variable. plan-stage estimates carry projectedGenerationCredits (upperBound: true), the ceiling if every alternate re-rendered every slide. {CREDIT_COSTS.experimentSlide} per slide render at generation: one render per slide, and slides an alternate shares with the baseline are free. A QA check of each deck ({CREDIT_COSTS.experimentPlanningCall}) is added, and estimate_experiment(stage="generate") gives the exact total. Experiment lifecycle: create_experiment (draft, free) → estimate_experiment stage=plan → user approves → plan_experiment (background: source analysis, pattern report, variant briefs) → status "review" → optionally update_experiment_variant → estimate_experiment stage=generate → user approves → generate_experiment (background slide rendering) → "completed". Approval: a spending step needs the user's OK, and a standing budget IS that OK. If the task or user granted a credit cap (per experiment or per batch), any estimate within the remaining cap is already approved: pass the remaining cap (or the estimate) as approvedCredits and run plan → generate without asking again. Without a cap, ask ONCE for all experiments and both stages together, not per experiment or per stage. Ask again only when an estimate exceeds what was approved. To change a brief, use update_experiment_variant (free) rather than cancel_experiment.

mode.description: "create" (default) = new variations from source videos plus instructions. "edit" = change overlay copy or character on one deck. "brief" = no source video: generate from instructions alone.

videoIds.description: Required in create and edit modes: 1–20 distinct Gallery video ids; one experiment per video. Edit mode takes exactly one. Must be omitted in brief mode.

instructions.description: CREATE and BRIEF modes. Required in both; rejected in edit mode (use top-level variables and character or hook/overlayTexts). Brief mode also requires instructions.direction.

variables.description: EDIT mode: ["hook"] for copy, ["character"] for casting only, ["scene"] for the setting, or ["morph"] (alias "ladder") to re-create a tier-ladder deck with one invented subject graded slide by slide, labels drawn in code. Defaults to scene when scene is supplied, then character when character is supplied, then morph when morph is supplied, otherwise hook.

scene.description: EDIT mode, scene variable: where the deck takes place instead (setting and props). One description for every slide, or an array with one per slide. Keeps the same person, outfit, pose, medium, lighting, camera and overlay text. Omit hook/overlayTexts/character.

morph.description: EDIT mode, morph variable: the progression to test in neutral visible words, optionally with per-slide grades 0-4 (e.g. "jaw definition 4,4,3,3,2,1,0; cheek fullness 0,0,1,2,3,3,4"). Omit to follow the source frames.

character.description: EDIT mode, character variable: visible casting changes (e.g. short blond hair). Keeps source copy, style, setting and story. Omit hook/overlayTexts.

hook.description: EDIT mode: the exact words for slide 1. OMIT this field to leave slide 1 unchanged; send an empty string only to strip slide 1's text.

overlayTexts.description: EDIT mode: overlay text for slides 2, 3, â¦ in order. Empty string = render no text on that slide. null = leave that slide's original text unchanged (use it to skip a slide between two you are editing).

language.description: EDIT mode: output language for the copy (default English).

overlayMode.description: EDIT mode: "script" renders slides text-free and composes the copy in code (use when the image provider rejects slides with a content-filter error). Default "model". In create mode use instructions.overlayMode.

variantCount.description: CREATE mode: variants per experiment, including the baseline (1–12). Edit mode is always 2.

slideCount.description: Slides per variant (3–8); overridden by the source deck length when known, minus a detected source CTA slide unless instructions.preserveSourceCtaSlide is true. Brief mode has no source deck, so this is exactly the output length.

maxCredits.description: Per-experiment credit ceiling (runaway guard). Default: the site's automatic cap, 2Ã the estimate rounded up; 200 in edit mode. An approved estimate may raise it.

composite.description: CREATE mode, photo-annotation sources (a face photo, a drawn line at a landmark, a ✅/❌ badge, a closing score card): shape the code-rendered deck. feature (jaw/ramus/…), subset (face-library ids), order (e.g. ["neg","pos","pos"]: cycled badge order and ratio), scoreCard {appName,name,score,tier}, seed. A named real person only ever appears on a ✅ slide. Hook text and the rest of the direction go in instructions.

tools.name: estimate_experiment
tools.description: Price the next step of an experiment before spending. Free. stage="plan" prices source analysis + planning (draft experiments); stage="generate" prices slide rendering for variantIds (default: all variants). Pass taskIds (from get_experiment progress.retryableJobs) to price retrying exactly those jobs. stage="revise" prices revise_experiment (the model rewrites the brief from the QA failures, then every arm is re-rendered). Returns totalCredits, the workspace wallet (workspaceCredits) and the experiment cap. If totalCredits is within a standing credit cap the user granted, it is already approved: pass the cap (or totalCredits) as approvedCredits to plan_experiment / generate_experiment / retry_experiment. Otherwise show totalCredits to the user and get a yes first (one request covering all experiments and both stages).

taskIds.description: Job ids to price a retry of.

tools.description: Start planning a DRAFT experiment: source analysis, pattern report, then variant briefs, all in the background. SPENDS CREDITS — call estimate_experiment(stage="plan") first. Pass as approvedCredits the amount already approved: the confirmed totalCredits, or under a standing credit cap (per experiment or per batch) the remaining cap, which counts as approval when the estimate is within it, so no extra confirmation is needed. Ask the user only when the estimate exceeds the approval. Afterwards status is "planning"; check with get_experiment until it reaches "review". The job ids it returns (experiment.jobs[].id) are NOT for await_job / get_job_status; track them with get_experiment.

tools.name: update_experiment_variant
tools.description: Edit one variant's brief. Free. Allowed only when the variant is a draft (never sent to generation, no frozen brief) and the experiment is: "review"; "completed" (for a draft variant that was not generated); or "failed"/"paused" while no provider job is running or unknown. Refused while "planning" or "generating" (experiment_active), when "cancelled" (experiment_cancelled), and in "draft" before planning has produced briefs (not_editable). A frozen or rendered variant is refused (variant_frozen). Pass the variant's current revision (get_experiment) â a stale revision is refused (revision_conflict), never overwritten. The brief must keep the experiment's slide count and lockedConstraints. Variants may differ only in the experiment's chosen variables (instructions.variables on get_experiment); every other brief field (e.g. cta, caption, character, visualStyle, concept, slides when not chosen) is shared. Edit a shared field on any ONE draft variant and the same change is applied to the other draft variants automatically, so retargeting the whole experiment (new topic, new copy) works one variant at a time; a chosen variable is edited per variant. If a shared field cannot be mirrored (another variant is frozen/rendered) or a variant would stop differing in a chosen variable, the edit is refused (422 unapproved_variable) and the message names the fields. Optional title and hypothesis rename the variant (not part of the brief). Returns the edited variant's new revision; any other variant that was updated gets a new revision too, so use the revisions in the result when calling generate_experiment.

tools.name: generate_experiment
tools.description: Render slide images for reviewed variants (status "review", or "completed" with draft variants left). SPENDS CREDITS — {CREDIT_COSTS.experimentSlide} per slide render (one render per slide; slides shared with the baseline are free), plus a QA check per deck ({CREDIT_COSTS.experimentPlanningCall}). Call estimate_experiment(stage="generate", variantIds) first. approvedCredits is the amount already approved: the confirmed totalCredits, or under a standing credit cap (per experiment or per batch) the remaining cap, which counts as approval when the estimate is within it. Ask the user only when the estimate exceeds it. Pass each variant with its CURRENT revision (get_experiment); the brief is frozen at that revision. Rendering runs in the background; check with get_experiment.

tools.name: retry_experiment
tools.description: Retry a failed or paused experiment. SPENDS CREDITS (retried jobs are charged again). Scope it with taskIds (from get_experiment progress.retryableJobs) or variantIds (failed slides of those variants); with neither, every failed job is retried and `stage` says how to price it (plan while no briefs exist yet, else generate). Call estimate_experiment with the same scope first. approvedCredits is the amount already approved: the confirmed totalCredits, or under a standing credit cap the remaining cap, which counts as approval when the estimate is within it. Ask the user only when it exceeds the approval. Prefer retry over cancel+recreate; completed images are kept.

stage.description: Pricing stage for a blanket retry (no taskIds/variantIds).

tools.name: revise_experiment
tools.description: Retry an experiment that FAILED QA by letting the model rewrite the brief. Use it when the experiment is failed and its slides were judged terminal QA failures (retry_experiment cannot fix those: it would only re-judge the same images). The QA failures of every arm are fed back to the contract model, which writes a corrected contract and briefs (the one tested variable stays the only difference between the arms); then all arms are re-rendered and QA-checked. SPENDS CREDITS: one planning call, a full re-render and QA of every arm. Call with estimateOnly:true first (free); approvedCredits is the amount the user approved (or the remaining standing cap). At most a few revisions per experiment. Track progress with get_experiment.

estimateOnly.description: Free: return the price, start nothing.

approvedCredits.description: Required unless estimateOnly. The credits the user approved for this revision.

tools.name: submit_experiment_feedback
tools.description: Give human feedback on a GENERATED slideshow (one variant) and regenerate it. `feedback` is about the whole slideshow and re-renders every slide; `slides` gives feedback for single slides (0-based index: slide 1 = 0) and re-renders only those (re-rendering the first slide of a one-person identity chain re-renders the later slides too, so the face stays the same). Pass either or both. Write what should change in the picture, e.g. "LTN still looks like MTN: make the jaw clearly softer and the face fuller". The notes stay attached to the slide, so later QA repairs of it keep them. The variant is then QA-checked again like a fresh render. SPENDS CREDITS: one slide render per re-rendered slide plus one QA call. Call it with estimateOnly:true first (free) to get the price and the slides it would redo; approvedCredits is the amount the user approved (or the remaining standing cap). Allowed when the experiment is completed, failed, paused or in review and no job of the variant is pending, running or unknown. Track progress with get_experiment.

tools.name: analyze_video
tools.description: Run AI analysis on a video. Uses the configured backend (default: gemini-native, fallback: gemini-text). gemini-native downloads the video via the active scraper (residential proxy, or Apify) then uploads it for native understanding (shots, audio, on-screen text); gemini-text does a text-only call on transcript + caption + metadata. Costs 5 credits. gemini-native is QUEUED rather than run inline — it cannot finish inside one request — so the response is a jobId and status, not an analysis. Wait for it with await_job (blocks server-side and returns the moment it finishes) rather than polling get_video in a loop; the analysisJob field on get_video still reports progress for a one-off check. gemini-text returns its analysis directly.
return_literals: Charged up front; refunded if the job fails before analysis starts.

MCP01.name: Token Mismanagement & Secret Exposure
MCP01.reason: Regex-based secret detection in server source and client configs plus env-var exposure checks; no entropy analysis, git-history scan, or token lifetime/passthrough checks.

MCP02.name: Privilege Escalation via Scope Creep
MCP02.reason: Permission over-scope patterns, toxic tool-capability combinations, path-escape checks and env-var over-exposure in configs.

MCP03.name: Tool Poisoning
MCP03.reason: Dedicated detector for hidden instructions in tool metadata, plus runtime rug-pull diffing between source and live tool definitions.

MCP04.name: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
MCP04.reason: Dependency CVE lookup, known MCP CVEs, install lifecycle hooks, and unpinned npx/uvx/pip/@latest install sources.

MCP05.name: Command Injection & Execution
MCP05.reason: Regex, AST and Semgrep find exec/shell sinks and a heuristic flags sinks inside tool handlers, but there is no inter-procedural taint tracking from tool input to sink.

MCP06.name: Prompt Injection via Contextual Payloads
MCP06.reason: Injection markers are detected in tool metadata, server instructions, resources, prompts and the strings a tool returns (static), and in instructions/resources/prompts read live; payloads produced by calling a tool at runtime are not inspected.

MCP07.name: Insufficient Authentication & Authorization
MCP07.reason: Flags remote servers with no visible auth and servers bound to all interfaces; does not verify OAuth implementation or per-tool authorization logic.

MCP08.name: Lack of Audit and Telemetry
MCP08.reason: Only a low-confidence heuristic for missing logging in tool-defining files; actual audit trails and telemetry pipelines are not verified.

MCP09.name: Shadow MCP Servers
MCP09.reason: Covered by `axiom discover` allowlist on the local machine; no network-wide or fleet discovery.

MCP10.name: Context Injection & Over-Sharing
MCP10.reason: Hard-coded egress URLs, tools that send to caller-chosen destinations and bulk-exposure heuristics are detected statically and live; what context is actually shared at runtime is not observed.
